Mark the student's response to a question from the 2024 NSW HSC Modern History exam strictly against the official marking criteria, exactly as an HSC marker would: award marks only for what is actually written, do not be generous, and quote the criteria row the response fits. Question 23(c) [12 marks]: How successful was resistance to apartheid within South Africa between 1960 and 1994?

MARKING CRITERIA (out of 12):
11–12 marks: Makes an insightful and sustained judgement about the success of the relevant feature | Uses detailed, specific, relevant and accurate historical information to support their judgement | Communicates ideas in a logical and well-structured form which uses a range of relevant historical terms and concepts appropriately
9–10 marks: Makes a well-reasoned judgement about the success of the relevant feature | Uses relevant and accurate historical information to support their judgement | Communicates ideas in a logical and structured form using relevant historical terms and concepts appropriately
6–8 marks: Makes a judgement about the success of the relevant feature | Uses relevant and accurate historical information | Communicates ideas in a logical and structured form using some historical terms and concepts
3–5 marks: Provides a description about the relevant feature | Uses some relevant historical detail including terms and concepts in their response
1–2 marks: Provides some relevant historical information


ANSWERS COULD INCLUDE (the student does not need every point):
The period from 1960 to 1994 was marked by intense resistance to apartheid in South Africa from different sectors from both within and outside of society. Their success was limited until the 1990s, when the cumulative effect of resistance finally led to the breakdown of Apartheid.
The apartheid system, which institutionalised racial segregation and discrimination, faced robust opposition from various groups within South Africa and globally during this time.
• The impact of Sharpeville and Soweto drawing international attention
• The global anti-apartheid movement including economic and diplomatic pressure
• ANC domestic strategies including non-violent protests and armed resistance
• Rivonia trial as a symbol of unity
• SACC and UDF mobilised communities and led to Soweto
• The role of key individuals including Mandela
• The differing approach of Steve Biko and the BCM.



STUDENT RESPONSE:
